applicant_utility.summary: Otago pays this as a $15,000 credit against tuition fees only, so the money never reaches your bank account and you still fund flights, insurance, accommodation and living costs yourself. You do not apply for it: you tick the agreement to be considered for international scholarships inside your eVision admission application and Otago assesses you as part of admission, so the dates that actually matter are the admission round closing dates. If you start in Semester 2 (July) the $15,000 is split $7,500/$7,500 across two enrolments, which changes your cash-flow planning. Because deferral is impossible, you must be able to start in the very semester you are offered.
applicant_utility.best_fit: School leavers holding one of the twelve nominated Asian passports who are certain they can begin on-campus undergraduate study at Otago in the intake they apply for.
application_readiness_checklist: Complete your eVision enrolment and tick the agreement to be considered for international scholarships - the scholarship assessment runs entirely off the admission application
Have final secondary results and a recognised University Entrance qualification ready before the admission deadline, since academic potential is judged from programme admission
Accept BOTH the admission offer and the separate scholarship offer letter by the deadline in that letter
Line up visa, funds and travel evidence so you can meet the enrolment date in your Offer of Place - the scholarship dies if you cannot start
Budget for the remaining tuition balance plus living costs: this is a tuition credit, not cash
Diary the offshore closing dates (10 December for a February start, 30 April for a July start) in your own calendar, as no separate scholarship reminder is issued
common_rejection_risks: Missing the offshore admission closing date for your intended start because there is no separate scholarship window to track
Being unable to commence by the enrolment date in the Offer of Place, which voids the scholarship and cannot be deferred
Accepting the admission offer but overlooking the scholarship offer letter's own acceptance deadline
Holding another Otago Undergraduate Entrance Scholarship - only the highest-value award is normally granted
Being sponsored by your home government or the New Zealand Government, which makes you ineligible outright
Enrolling into a foundation certificate programme, which is specifically excluded
Applying from a nominated country without actually holding one of the twelve listed passports, since selection turns on the passport
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, international flights, medical insurance, accommodation and the balance of tuition - Otago states the award is a credit towards tuition fees only, and scholarships under these terms normally cannot cover accommodation acceptance fees, insurance or other sundry fees.
document_audit: The eVision scholarship-consent tick box is the only application step; there is no essay, CV or reference to supply for this award
Academic transcripts must evidence University Entrance and are assessed through admission, so missing or untranslated documents delay the offer and the scholarship with it
The passport is the decisive document: eligibility is framed around applying from a nominated country, but selection is explicitly on those who hold one of the twelve listed passports
If you completed secondary school or foundation study in New Zealand, the route changes to the Entrance Scholarship application between 1 July and 15 August, not the eVision agreement
Watch for multiple Offers of Place - they signal eligibility, not multiple awards, since only one scholarship is formally awarded
alerts: Deferral of the scholarship is not possible - a gap year means being reassessed for a later cycle
Semester 2 (July) starters get half now and half next February, so the credit does not settle your first-year fees in one hit
Otago reserves the right to amend the nominated countries and programmes of study lists at its discretion
If your residency status changes from international to domestic during tenure, the University may suspend or terminate the scholarship and require return of funds in part or in full
Withdrawing, stopping study, or terminating enrolment cancels entitlement and can trigger repayment of funds already paid
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the eVision application for study with the scholarship agreement ticked; Otago assesses automatically during admission, then you must actively accept both the admission offer and the scholarship offer letter by its stated deadline.

applicant_utility.summary: This is Otago's entrance tuition credit for any new international undergraduate, with no country list, so a much wider pool competes for the smaller $10,000. Mechanically it works exactly like the Global Scholarship - no separate application, assessed during admission, accepted via the offer letter - but the lower value leaves a larger self-funded gap. Because Otago normally grants only the highest-value Undergraduate Entrance Scholarship you hold, this is often the baseline award that then earns you an invitation to apply for the competitive $35,000 International Academic Excellence Scholarship after you accept it.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Any new international undergraduate applicant to Otago who meets University Entrance and can start in the offered semester, especially applicants outside the twelve nominated countries who cannot access the Global Scholarship.
